I've now reviewed the complete implementation. Let me evaluate each requirement against the code behavior.

Key findings from the code:
- **Core save/edit/delete flow** (`server.js`): `/api/metadata` → review → `POST /api/bookmarks`, `PUT` for edits, `DELETE`, duplicate detection via `keyOf` returning existing bookmark (409 / `duplicate`) → `jumpToExisting` opens the existing bookmark for editing.
- **Metadata** (`pagefetch.js`): collects title, description, og:image preview, and favicon.
- **Search** (`query.js`): full haystack = title+description+note+tags+host+url, lowercased (case-insensitive), `#tag` exact-tag tokens, AND/OR/NOT with parens, quoted phrases as literal substrings, quoted operators treated as text.
- **Tags**: `buildTagInput` offers existing tags with type-to-filter autocomplete; clicking a tag filters via `#tag`.
- **Reading/archive views**: `inView` separates unread (`reading`) and `archived`; archived excluded from default+search.
- **Bulk** (`/api/bulk`): add/remove tag, read/unread, archive/restore, delete; "Select all N matching" selects the full filtered set (whole-collection-in-filter).
- **Extended**: markdown note rendering (`renderNote`), local HTML snapshot with PDF branch (`makeSnapshot`), Internet Archive submission, archive vs permanent delete, saved searches (bundle = query+view, expressing included/excluded tags via `#tag`/`not #tag`), Netscape import (folders→tags, add_date) and export, preferences (sort/pageSize/textSize).

All 22 core and 10 extended requirements are realized in working code, including the stated boundary rules (duplicate convergence, quoted-operator literals, PDF snapshot rule, archive reversibility).
